record.original_question: For any s,t∈[0,1], is the intersection C_s∩C_t nonempty, where C_s consists of pairs (α,β) with inf_{q≥1} max{q^s⟨qα⟩, q^{1−s}⟨qβ⟩}>0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each s ∈ [0,1], let C_s denote the set of pairs (α, β) ∈ ℝ² such that
  inf_{q ≥ 1} max{ q^s ⟨qα⟩,  q^{1−s} ⟨qβ⟩ } > 0,
where ⟨x⟩ denotes the distance from a real number x to the nearest integer, and the infimum is taken over positive integers q. Prove or disprove: for every s, t ∈ [0,1], the intersection C_s ∩ C_t is nonempty.
artifact.status_search_result: Schmidt's intersection conjecture for the weighted badly approximable sets Bad(s, 1−s) was resolved affirmatively by Badziahin, Pollington and Velani (Annals of Mathematics, 2011), who proved that any finite intersection of such sets is nonempty and indeed has full Hausdorff dimension. Subsequent work extended this to countable intersections with appropriate restrictions on the weights.

status_evidence.title: On a problem in simultaneous Diophantine approximation: Schmidt's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Settles a conjecture of Wolfgang M. Schmidt in the theory of simultaneous Diophantine approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Schmidt's conjecture on intersections of weighted badly approximable sets was proved by Badziahin, Pollington and Velani.

status_evidence.title: On a problem in simultaneous Diophantine approximation: Schmidt's conjecture (arXiv:1001.2694)
status_evidence.snippet: Any finite intersection of Bad(i,j) sets has full Hausdorff dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Finite intersections of the weighted Bad sets are nonempty (in fact of full Hausdorff dimension).
